descriptionChirho: A person who is foreign, alien, or an outsider — used substantively or attributively of people who do not belong to the community or family.
Specifically the 'strange woman' of Proverbs wisdom literature — a foreign or adulterous woman whose ways lead to ruin.
Applied to non-persons — strange gods, strange things, foreign or unfamiliar objects and concepts.
In the Qal stem, to become estranged, alienated, or to turn away from someone or something.
In the Nifal stem, to be or become estranged in a reflexive or passive sense — to withdraw, fall away, or turn back.
